title: K-injective normalization and derived adjunction at an identity open locus
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. All schemes are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible commutative condensed coefficient [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Use the small pro-etale sites in the coefficient universe, the internal module categories $\Mod_{\Lambda_T}$, and the specified module pullback/direct-image adjunctions $f^*\dashv f_*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback, def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]. Their pullbacks are exact [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main]. Let $h:D\to Z$, let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ be a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and specify $h^{-1}(U)\cong U$ over $U$, with resulting open inclusion $i:U\hookrightarrow D$ and $hi=j$. No properness or density is assumed. Write $c_h:j^*h_*\cong i^*$ for the sectionwise comparison whose value at every pro-etale $T\to U$ is the identity on $M(T\to U\xrightarrow{i}D)$. Write $a_h:i^*h^*\cong j^*$ for the inverse of the composition comparison [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] for $hi=j$, using the canonical identity-pullback identification.

Assume the underived comparisons respect adjuncts in the precise sense that for every $t:h^*M\to N$ one has $c_{h,N}\circ j^*(t^\sharp)=i^*(t)\circ a_{h,M}^{-1}$, where $t^\sharp$ is the adjunct for the specified adjunction. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$, the total derived functors and their canonical adjunction $h^*\dashv Rh_*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Here an exact pullback denotes its termwise derived functor, and $a_h$ also denotes its termwise derived comparison.

Let $r_h:j^*Rh_*\cong i^*$ be the canonical natural restriction isomorphism of [lem-sfb-identity-open-derived-restriction] for $(Z',j')=(D,i)$; its hypotheses $hi=j$ and $h^{-1}(j(U))=i(U)$ hold by the specified identification. It has the following resolution normalization. For every K-injective resolution $P\to I$ on the small ringed-site module model [def-pur-kinjective-complex, lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport], it is represented by $c_{h,I}:j^*h_*I\cong i^*I$, followed by the inverse of the restricted resolution quasi-isomorphism identifying $i^*I$ with $i^*P$. The exact internal-to-sectionwise equivalence preserves K-injectivity, and the restriction $i^*I$ is K-injective. No image of $I$ under any additional non-open pullback is assumed K-injective.

Write $Q$ for localization of complexes and $\gamma_{h,P}:Q(h_*P)\to Rh_*(QP)$ for the right-derived comparison unit [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. The normalization satisfies
$$r_{h,QP}\circ j^*(\gamma_{h,P})=Q(c_{h,P}),$$
using the canonical exact-functor localization identifications. In particular $j^*Rh_*$, with this localized comparison unit, is a total right derived functor of $j^*h_*$. For the actual derived adjunction unit $\eta_h$ and counit $\varepsilon_h$, the following equalities hold for every $A\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Z})$ and $K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_D})$:
$$r_{h,h^*A}\circ j^*(\eta_{h,A})=a_{h,A}^{-1},\qquad i^*(\varepsilon_{h,K})=r_{h,K}\circ a_{h,Rh_*K}.$$
These equalities are natural in $A,K$ and use the specified derived adjunction, rather than an independently chosen adjunction on isomorphic functors.

proof.text: Use the additive exact equivalences $E_T$ of [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport], which identify the specified operations and adjunctions with the sectionwise ringed-site ones. They preserve and reflect K-injectivity: an acyclic complex $C$ in the target pulls back to an acyclic complex $E_T^{-1}C$, and the degreewise equivalence identifies chain maps and their homotopies, giving $\operatorname{Hom}_K(C,E_TI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_K(E_T^{-1}C,I)=0$ for K-injective $I$; apply the inverse equivalence for reflection. The small-site hypothesis is part of the statement. Thus [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] applies to the reconstructed section-ring sheaves and transports K-injective resolutions to the internal categories. The comparison of adjunctions includes their actual units and counits, so this transport does not introduce a different adjunction.

source.place: Tag 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open: sectionwise model; Section 07A5, section-unbounded: existence of K-injective resolutions; transport through the cited exact equivalence

proof.text: The module pullbacks $i^*,j^*,h^*$ are exact and additive by [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main]. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] they preserve quasi-isomorphisms and descend termwise with the canonical localization identifications. For the open $i$, [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] states both $i_!\dashv i^*$ and exactness of $i_!$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] to $u=i^*$ and $v=i_!$: both are additive, $v$ is exact, and $u$ is its right adjoint. Hence $i^*I$ is K-injective whenever $I$ is. This uses the open left adjoint, not an assertion about arbitrary non-open inverse images.

proof.text:
The specified identification $h^{-1}(U)\cong U$ makes $i$ quasi-compact (it is the base change of $j$, by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change]) and gives $hi=j$ and $h^{-1}(j(U))=i(U)$, so [lem-sfb-identity-open-derived-restriction] applies with $Z'=D,j'=i$. Its sectionwise identity is exactly the prescribed $c_h$. Let $s:P\to I$ be any K-injective resolution. By [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], $\gamma_{h,I}$ is invertible, and the canonical evaluation isomorphism is $d_s=\gamma_{h,I}^{-1}\circ Rh_*(Qs):Rh_*(QP)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(h_*I)$. The cited restriction lemma says $r_{h,QI}=Q(c_{h,I})\circ j^*(\gamma_{h,I})^{-1}$. Naturality of its $r_h$ at $Qs$, followed by inversion of $Q(i^*s)$, therefore gives
$$r_{h,QP}=Q(i^*s)^{-1}\circ Q(c_{h,I})\circ j^*(d_s).$$
This is the claimed normalization on every resolution, with $i^*I$ K-injective by step 2; its independence and naturality use the already natural $r_h$, rather than any additional choice of maps between resolutions.

source.place: Tag 0D6G, lemma-restrict-direct-image-open, K-injective computation; derived.tex Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined, for evaluation via the canonical comparison unit

proof.text:
Naturality of the right-derived comparison unit [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] for $s:P\to I$ gives
$$Rh_*(Qs)\circ\gamma_{h,P}=\gamma_{h,I}\circ Q(h_*s),\qquad d_s\circ\gamma_{h,P}=Q(h_*s).$$
Substitute this into step 3 and use the termwise naturality equation $c_{h,I}\circ j^*(h_*s)=i^*(s)\circ c_{h,P}$. With the exact-functor localization identifications, the result is
$$r_{h,QP}\circ j^*(\gamma_{h,P})=Q(i^*s)^{-1}\circ Q(i^*s)\circ Q(c_{h,P})=Q(c_{h,P}).$$
The cancellation is valid because $i^*$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms, as in step 2. This holds for arbitrary $P$, which need not itself be K-injective.

source.place: Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined, and Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; explicit naturality computation for the derived comparison unit

proof.text: Since $c_h:j^*h_*\cong i^*$ and $i^*$ is exact, $Q(j^*h_*(-))$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms. The localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] says that its descent $D(i^*)$, with comparison $Q(c_h)$, is a total right derived pair: for every functor $G$ out of the derived category, full faithfulness of precomposition with $Q$ identifies natural transformations $D(i^*)\to G$ with transformations $D(i^*)Q\to GQ$; precomposition with the isomorphism $Q(c_h)$ then gives precisely transformations $Q(j^*h_*(-))\to GQ$. Step 4 identifies the pair $(j^*Rh_*,j^*\gamma_h)$ with that pair through $r_h$. Consequently $(j^*Rh_*,j^*\gamma_h)$ has the required total right derived universal property, with the specified unit.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; localization at quasi-isomorphisms and its fully faithful precomposition, as stated by the cited universal-property node

proof.text:
Apply [lem-kun-derived-adjoint-square-comparison] with $\mathcal A=\Mod_{\Lambda_D}$, $\mathcal B=\Mod_{\Lambda_Z}$, $\mathcal A_0=\mathcal B_0=\Mod_{\Lambda_U}$, $(L,R)=(h^*,h_*)$, $(L_0,R_0)=(1,1)$ with the identity adjunction, $V=i^*$, $W=j^*$, $a=a_h$ and $c=c_h$. The specified underived adjunction is [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]. Its compatibility condition is exactly the adjunct equation assumed here. Exactness of $L,V,W$ is step 2; $L_0$ is exact. The canonical total derived adjunction for $h$ is [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]; its left adjoint $Lh^*$ is the total left derived functor of the exact $h^*$, which the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] identifies with the termwise $D(h^*)=D(L)$ of the square theorem, so this is the derived adjunction $D(L)\dashv RR$ of the specified $h^*\dashv h_*$ that the theorem uses; the identity functor and its identity comparison descend to the identity adjunction. The remaining right-derived hypothesis on $D(W)RR$ is step 5. In this specialization the comparison $b$ is characterized by $b_{QP}j^*(\gamma_{h,P})=Q(c_{h,P})$. By step 4 and the universal property in step 5, this is precisely $r_h$. The two unit and counit equations of the square theorem, with the identity unit and counit removed, are
$$r_{h,h^*A}\circ j^*(\eta_{h,A})=a_{h,A}^{-1},\qquad i^*(\varepsilon_{h,K})=r_{h,K}\circ a_{h,Rh_*K}.$$
That theorem asserts these for the canonical derived adjunctions and as natural equations. It therefore proves both identities for exactly the adjunction specified here.
